clue.text: Kind heart of Malaysian getting warmer?

parts.note: a kind or make of product is a brand

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, here of Malaysian

explanation.surface: A kindly Malaysian person warms up to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of' takes the middle letter, Y, of the nine-letter Malaysian.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit such as cognac is drunk to warm a person up, hence the question mark on this playful description.

clue.text: Sax was being almost all jazzy?

indicators.note: jazzy suggests the letters are jazzed up and improvised into a new order
almost means the word all loses its final letter

explanation.surface: The saxophone was nearly always jazzy.
explanation.walkthrough: Sax is Adolphe Sax, the inventor of the saxophone, who came from Dinant in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Adolphe Sax, who gave his name to the saxophone, was a native of Belgium.

clue.text: So far away several yetis entering Tibet's most westerly extremes

indicators.note: in a down entry read across, the westerly end of each word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Yetis have so far ranged as far as Tibet's western borders.
explanation.definitionFit: As yet means up to now, so far, until this moment.

clue.text: Drop tray, emptied onto church's work of art

parts.note: to drop is to dip

indicators.note: an emptied word has its inside letters removed, leaving the ends

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone drops a tray onto a church's art treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emptied' leaves only the outer letters of tray, TY.
explanation.definitionFit: A diptych is a painting on two hinged panels, often an altarpiece in a church.

clue.text: Seal broken by force at first, before I look

indicators.note: the seal is broken open so a letter sits inside it

parts.note: to seal something is to shut it

indicators.note: only the opening letter of force is used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A seal is forced open before someone takes a peek.
explanation.walkthrough: SHUFTI is British army slang, from Arabic, for a quick look.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a shufti is British slang for taking a quick glance or peek at something.

clue.text: Earth: then what rises? The Sun!

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means reading upwards, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: earth meaning ground or dirt is soil
eh? is a way of asking what?

explanation.surface: First comes the Earth, then what rises over it but the Sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Helios is the Greek god of the sun, who drove its chariot across the sky.

clue.text: This in fact not half a distortion of reality?

definitions.text: This in fact not half a distortion of reality?

indicators.note: only half of the word fact is used, its first two letters
a distortion twists the letters of reality into another order

explanation.surface: A fantasy story warps the real world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' leaves FA; 'distortion of' scrambles REALITY into IRYTALE. The whole clue loosely defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanciful story of magic and enchantment is far from fact and distorts reality.

clue.text: Where you may see reindeer I see antelope

parts.note: taken as written
the letter C is spoken like the word see
the eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A visitor spots an antelope among the reindeer.
explanation.definitionFit: Reindeer were introduced to the island nation in the North Atlantic and still roam its east.

clue.text: Upset tabloid concealing dread, rubbished paper as aggressive performer

indicators.note: one piece hides another within it
in a down entry upset turns the word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a tabloid newspaper
angst is anxiety or dread

indicators.note: rubbished means trashed, so the letters of paper are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A tabloid hides its fear, trashing a paper over a violent musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performer' suggests a stage actor, but the clue wants a rap artist; 'Upset' reads the tabloid word upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangsta rap is a hip-hop style with violent lyrics, so its performers are aggressive musicians.

clue.text: See 16
Criminal prevailed before ending in slammer, one going down for a long time

definitions.text: one going down for a long time

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters of prevailed are twisted out of their lawful order
only the final letter of slammer is taken

explanation.surface: A crook beat the rap, then landed in prison for a long stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going down for a long time' sounds like a prison sentence, but it means diving deep and holding the breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dives for oysters must stay underwater a long while, gathering shells that may hold gems.

clue.text: Take gold and go cold

parts.note: to take gold in a contest is to win
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: An athlete wins a medal and then the weather turns chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: Wintry weather is cold, as in winter; the adjective is a synonym of chilly.

clue.text: Annus mirabilis for the rubber man

definitions.meaning: Latin for a year of wonders, that is a year in which things went well
Charles ..., the American who invented vulcanised rubber

explanation.surface: A rubber manufacturer enjoys a marvellous twelve months.
explanation.definitionFit: A year of wonders is a fine twelvemonth, and Charles Goodyear pioneered vulcanised rubber, his name now a tyre brand.

clue.text: 6's pretty flaky character?

parts.note: a heroine of a fairy tale, the fairest of them all and named after the white flakes of winter

explanation.surface: A fairy tale's charming but unreliable heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flaky' suggests unreliable, but points to snowflakes; 'pretty' is the mirror's verdict that she is fairest of all.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grimm heroine whose skin is white as snow is the beautiful central character of a famous fairy tale.

clue.text: Incoherent speech, so a drawl collapsed and died

indicators.note: collapsed signals the letters fall apart and are rebuilt

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A speaker's slow drawl gave out and the speaker died.
explanation.definitionFit: Word salad is a jumble of words with no logical connection, a sign of some mental disorders.

clue.text: Comedian, one in a suit?

definitions.meaning: a joker or wag, a funny person
a member of a suit such as hearts or spades in a pack

explanation.surface: A comic turns up wearing formal clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A card is a witty, amusing person, and every playing card belongs to one of four suits.

clue.text: Bit of fun with possible role to impress partner, initially — later a 23 26?

definitions.text: Bit of fun with possible role to impress partner, initially — later a 23 26?

indicators.note: only a small piece, the first letter, of fun is taken
to impress is to press a letter into, so one piece sits inside the other
possible signals that the letters of role could be arranged another way
the opening letter of partner only
the clue 26 means ending, so the final letter is taken

parts.note: the clue 23 gives the word for cheerful, a dwarf's name

explanation.surface: Playful lovemaking before the satisfying conclusion of the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' rearranges ROLE to OREL, and 'to impress' sets P inside it; '26' (ending) takes the last letter of 23 (HAPPY). The whole clue is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexual play before intercourse is fun with a partner, and it comes before the climax the clue cheekily calls a 23 26.

clue.text: Pay on time for some film

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Paying for time on a film shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' means placed after in a down entry; to foot a bill is British usage for paying it.
explanation.definitionFit: Footage is a length of recorded film, some of a film's material.

clue.text: How often what needs translating into another language not entirely okay in the end

indicators.note: one piece goes inside another
the language name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: French is a foreign language
the word what, translated into French, is que

indicators.note: only the final letter of okay is taken

explanation.surface: A translator asks how often an expression must be put into a foreign tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what needs translating' asks for the French word for what; 'not entirely' drops the language name's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Frequency is the rate at which something happens, so it answers the question how often.

clue.text: In which 16 9, say?

parts.note: 16 9 is foreplay, which said aloud sounds like four play, describing a musical group of four

explanation.surface: Where, say, intimacy takes place.
explanation.definitionFit: A quartet is an ensemble of four musicians who perform together.

clue.text: Order, no doubt for starters

parts.note: the punctuation mark after the first word is itself called a comma

indicators.note: the starting letter of each of the two words before

explanation.surface: Giving an order, no doubt to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed punctuation mark supplies COMMA, an unusual device.
explanation.definitionFit: A command is an order, an instruction that must be obeyed.

clue.text: Tension in the air

explanation.surface: Stress hanging in the atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Strain is stress or tension, and a strain is also a passage of melody, an air.

clue.text: With sound method pack it in roof

indicators.note: signals that the letters entered are spoken like the words that follow

parts.note: method is how and pack it in is stop, so together the words say how stop

explanation.surface: A builder with a sound approach tells a roofer to give up.
explanation.definitionFit: A housetop is the roof of a building, the very top of the house.

clue.text: In a book, heroic opening captured

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the book takes the letter prisoner, holding it within

parts.note: a tome is a large book

indicators.note: the first letter of heroic only

explanation.surface: A heroic tale's opening episode is told within a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in is to be at home, as when someone answers that the family are in this evening.

clue.text: 13 has one, as a friend of hers is dying

parts.note: Happy is one of the seven dwarfs who befriend the heroine
something ending is dying away

explanation.surface: Snow White has one, as one of her friends lies at death's door.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is Snow White, whose seven dwarf companions include one named Happy.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairy tales such as Snow White traditionally conclude with everyone living contentedly ever after.

clue.text: Creator of life inspiring Irishman in assembly

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one word takes another inside it

parts.note: a parent brings a child into the world
Liam is a common Irish male first name

explanation.surface: A creative force motivates an Irishman sitting in a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A legislative assembly, such as the one at Westminster, is a parliament.

clue.text: Hot stuff seen in photograph album

indicators.note: the letters can be seen running through the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something steamy is spotted in someone's photo album.
explanation.walkthrough: PHAL (phall) is a fiercely hot curry from British Indian restaurants.
explanation.definitionFit: Phal is reputed to be the hottest curry on a British Indian menu, hotter than vindaloo.

clue.text: See 23
Remained proper, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the letters entered are spoken the same as the word for proper

parts.note: staid means sedate, respectable and proper

explanation.surface: Someone stayed on, to all appearances well behaved.
explanation.definitionFit: To have stayed is to have remained in a place rather than leaving.
